label: 平場戦
note: JRA explicitly gives 平場戦 as another name for 一般競走.

label: 平場
note: JRA defines 平場 as non-special races/general conditions races.

label: 斤量
note: Current synonym for 負担重量 with historical origin in the 斤 unit.

label: カンパイ
note: JRA stable-language term for restarting after an invalid start.

label: 道悪
note: JRA uses it for 重 or worse; not a formal fifth track-condition grade.

label: 攻め馬
note: JRA defines 攻め馬 as horse training; stronger pre-race work is 追い切り.

label: Bumper
note: BHA says National Hunt Flat races are also known as Bumpers; RTYPE-005 remains related to RTYPE-006.

label: Bumpers
note: Current IHRB safety-limits page uses Bumpers operationally.

label: Locked In
note: Canadian harness alias mapped to Boxed In.

label: Exactor
note: Canadian harness regional name for Exacta.

label: Perfecta
note: Alternative regional name for Exacta.

label: Triactor
note: Canadian regional name for Trifecta.

label: ガレる
note: JRA: weight loss, poor coat and reduced condition. Review whether this merits a standalone horse-condition Concept.

label: 口取り
note: JRA gives at least two senses: handling a horse by the mouth/head for gate/control, and winner's-circle commemorative photography. Do not collapse without sense split.

label: 鉄砲
note: Long-layoff first run / use after a relatively long break. Not identical to the layoff period itself.

label: 一本かぶり
note: Overwhelming concentration of betting support on one horse or combination; review as a betting-market concept.

label: ヒモ
note: Partner/other selection relative to a key horse; historical nuance noted by JRA.

label: Chalk
note: Established North American slang for the betting favorite.

label: Bomb
note: Current fan/racing-media slang for a huge longshot.

label: Chalk player
note: Bettor who wagers on favorites; usage is established, but the master lacks a general bettor/person Concept family.

label: Bridge jumper
note: Person who wagers very large sums on short-priced horses, often to show, seeking a small return. Candidate person/betting-behaviour Concept.

label: Rabbit
note: Speed horse entered with another horse, usually to create pace for a stablemate; needs a tactical-role Concept rather than being mapped to generic Pacesetter.

label: racebike
note: Standardbred Canada states the sulky is also known as the cart or racebike.

label: taking the overland route
note: Standardbred Canada gives this as an alternate description of Parked Out.

label: sidewheeler
note: Standardbred Canada says pacers are also referred to as sidewheelers; review a horse/gait-type Concept instead of mapping to the Pacing discipline itself.

label: お手馬
note: Horse repeatedly ridden by one jockey who knows its traits well; likely a jockey-horse relationship Concept.

label: 親子どんぶり
note: Same owner or stable supplies two or more runners and takes first and second; likely an outcome/connection-pattern Concept.

label: ズブい
note: Horse slow to respond/accelerate and requiring persistent urging; not equivalent to a running style.

label: ソラを使う
note: Horse loses concentration during racing or training; likely horse-behaviour Concept.

label: 馬っ気
note: Colloquial term for sexual arousal in a male horse; consider horse-condition/behaviour domain.

label: réclamers
note: France Galop explicitly uses “réclamers” for courses à réclamer; map to Claiming race while retaining French auction mechanics in the jurisdiction definition.

label: gentlemen-rider
note: France Galop uses gentlemen-rider for a male rider authorized in amateur races.

label: cavalière
note: France Galop defines cavalière as a female jockey authorized to ride in amateur races.

label: monter aux bras
note: Jockey urges a horse through the arms/neck without resorting to the whip; candidate riding-technique Concept.

label: courir caché
note: Horse is kept behind other runners to conserve its chance for the finish; not identical to generic hold-up horse.

label: nez au vent
note: Horse races without another runner in front and therefore without aerodynamic cover; candidate position/tactical state.

label: train
note: France Galop defines train as the speed at which a race is run; maps cleanly to Pace in French racing context.

label: faux train
note: Deliberately slow/false pace imposed by the leader to preserve its chance; more specific than generic Pace.

label: train de sénateur
note: Idiomatic French expression for a very slow pace; should be related to Pace but not promoted as its preferred label.

label: crack
note: France Galop defines crack as an exceptional horse; candidate horse-quality Concept rather than a class/rating term.

label: musique
note: French term for compact recent-results notation such as 7p5p2s0h1p; ordering differs from GB/IRE, so needs a dedicated form-notation Concept.

label: leader
note: France Galop uses leader for a horse tasked with setting a strong pace to help a horse sharing interests; semantically close to North American Rabbit but not yet asserted exact-equivalent.

label: roughie
note: Australian term for a horse at a long price with a lower perceived chance; maps to Longshot.

label: hoop
note: Racing Victoria explicitly gives Hoop as another name for a jockey.

label: stipes
note: Racing Victoria gives Stipes as shorthand for stipendiary stewards.

label: mudlark
note: Horse that excels on wet tracks; not equivalent to a track-condition Concept because it describes horse aptitude.

label: backed off the map
note: Heavy betting support on a horse; review betting-market-movement/concentration ontology.

label: stone motherless
note: Clear last-place finisher; candidate result/margin expression, not merely Last Place.

label: under double wraps
note: Horse travelling strongly without urging; candidate running-state expression.

label: mug punter
note: Colloquial term for a poor bettor/punter; reinforces need to decide whether bettor-person roles belong in the public ontology.

label: Stipe
note: Current NZ careers material states a Stipendiary Steward is often called a Stipe.

label: Jumpouts
note: NZ guide uses Jumpouts for barrier-gate practice below the level of official trials; extends Jump-out Concept into NZ usage.

label: Spelling
note: NZ guide uses Spelling for a recuperative break from training/racing; map to Spell.

label: greenly
note: Describes an inexperienced horse behaving erratically/hesitantly in a race; candidate behaviour/performance Concept.

label: on the bit/bridle
note: Horse travels seemingly easily without much urging; concept boundary with travelling strongly/under restraint needs review.

label: off the bit/bridle
note: Opposite of on the bit/bridle; horse is being asked to operate at or near maximum effort.

label: 3/4 Pace
note: Training-effort shorthand for roughly three-quarters of race/gallop speed; candidate training-intensity Concept.

label: Half Pace
note: Training-effort shorthand for approximately half race/gallop speed.

label: Mudlark
note: Current NZ jumps glossary also uses Mudlark for a horse thriving in wet/heavy conditions, corroborating Australasian usage.

label: landing gear
note: Current NZ jumps glossary slang for a horse’s legs; useful reader term but likely a register-only label rather than a standalone racing Concept.
